 Detailed Forecast
 Synopsis
 A high pressure system northeast of the Hawaiian Islands will continue to drift eastward and weaken. Two passing upper level disturbances will keep wet trade wind weather in the forecast through the end of this week. The subtropical ridge will settle in over the island chain by early next week with a drying trend forecast.
 Discussion
 A low level trough has settled south of the state this afternoon. Showers have decreased in coverage and intensity across the northern islands, but continue farther south. The 00Z sounding from Lihue shows a clear drying trend in the boundary layer with an inversion height falling from 9kft to 7kft today, indicting ridging is building back.
A mid/upper level trough about 500 miles west of Kauai this afternoon will progress east and weaken some tonight and Wednesday. Nonetheless, inversion heights will rise a bit again as this feature swings through, and trade showers will continue mostly in the typical areas. Some spillover into the leeward zones is also possible at times.
Reinforcing surface high pressure will arrive north of the state Thursday night and Friday. An uptick in higher elevation wind appears likely Thursday night into Friday, but at this time speeds look to remain just below advisory criteria. Otherwise, daily shower coverage will be dependent on pockets of deeper moisture passing through in the trade flow this weekend.
Mid level ridging will build over and to the west of the islands early next week. Inversion heights will fall to around or just below 850 mb, or 4-5kft. That, and decreasing low level moisture, will allow for drier conditions and lower shower coverage. Any showers should be confined to windward and mountain areas early next week.
 Aviation
 Moderate to breezy trade winds will continue into Wednesday with isolated showers possible in windward and mountain areas. Expect MVFR ceilings and visibilities in any passing showers which could spill over to leeward locations at times.
AIRMET Sierra remains in effect above 2000 feet for north through east sections of the Big Island due to lingering low clouds and showers.
AIRMET Tango remains in effect below 7000 feet for low level moderate turbulence over and downwind of island mountains.
 Marine
 Trade winds will ease slightly over the next few days. A Small Craft Advisory (SCA) is in effect through Thursday for the typically windy waters around Big Island and Maui as a series of highs and fronts quickly pass well north of Hawaii. Trades will strengthen again late Thursday and Friday as a stronger high passes north of the state, then drop a notch during the weekend.
A moderate, medium-period north (010 degrees) swell will gradually decline through Wednesday. Expect north shore surf on all islands to slowly decline today and fade late Wednesday. A small north-northwest swell will be possible during the weekend, with a larger swell possible next Tuesday.
Rough surf along east-facing shores will drop to seasonal average tonight as winds slightly taper and the north swell declines. A slight increase in east shore surf is expected Friday and Saturday. Mainly small background level surf will persist along south-facing shores during the next several days, with a small long-period swell possible on Friday.
 Fire weather
 A wet trade wind pattern lasting into the weekend will keep humidity levels below critical fire thresholds for most of the windier areas for the next several days. Temperature inversion heights near Maui and the Big Island this afternoon are around 9 kft but are expected to drop to 6-7 kft Wednesday.
 HFO Watches/Warnings/Advisories
 Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST Thursday for Alenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters, Big Island Southeast Waters, Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel.
